product.name: OpenState
product.category: Local developer tool for coding agents
product.short_description: OpenState provides guarded structural code-search, reading and editing, alongside a persistent local record of project decisions, failures and blockers.
product.positioning: Two equal capabilities: precise structural code operations and continuity of project state across sessions.
product.target_audience: Developers doing sustained work with local coding agents, especially in repositories with repeated sessions and edits.
not_for: A replacement for tests or code review
product.source_policy: Human pages are the concise product and sales explanation. This file is the machine-readable, expanded description of the same facts—not a separate set of claims.

elevator_summary: The agent finds a function, reads that definition, previews an exact edit, and writes only after the preview passes. Separately, OpenState derives project facts from session events and makes a short context capsule available in later sessions. OpenCode injects the capsule natively; other MCP clients request it on demand.

Unlimited structural applies for one developer, on up to 3 machines while subscription is paid.

licensing.shared_capabilities: Same code tools, state tools and engine in free and paid editions; the structural apply count is the paid distinction.
licensing.metering: A successful structural *_apply is one use, even if it writes several files. Read, search, and preview operations do not consume uses. Refused or failed writes do not count.
licensing.payments: Stripe handles checkout; Keygen issues and validates licenses through an OpenState Cloudflare worker.
licensing.refund_statement: All sales are final, subject to applicable law; review the binding terms and refund policy before purchasing.
licensing.update_scope_warning: The word lifetime in a checkout route denotes the 0.x product-line license, not guaranteed access to every future major version.
licensing.offline_grace_paid: Up to 7 days between successful license checks.
licensing.monthly_to_one_time: Supported through the licensing worker; charges the full one-time price, preserves the key, and cancels the monthly subscription. Unused month is not credited.

capabilities.supported_language_note: The published claim is 18 language families; TSX is included with TypeScript. Exact operations depend on language grammar and tool, and Rust diagnostics apply only to Rust.
capabilities.structural_engine: ast-grep-backed lexical AST navigation/editing plus a Rust commit boundary for validated writes.
write_contract: Searches, readers and previews do not write project files.
Apply is an explicit, separate operation and uses the returned preview identity.
A consumed preview cannot be applied a second time.
Edits refuse stale source or ambiguous targeting as appropriate.
The engine checks the write contract before committing files; refusal is preferable to overwriting incompatible state.
Syntactic guardrails do not prove semantic correctness; tests and review remain necessary.
session_state: Records objectives, reason-bearing decisions and directives, attempted commands and observed outcomes, active work, blockers, relevant paths and available test state.
Captures only events accessible to the host or replay adapter; it does not observe model reasoning, external shell activity or every hidden host event.
Facts are retractable or superseded as subsequent observations change what is known; inspect provenance using openstate_why.
State is local and repository-scoped; no built-in multi-machine or team synchronization.
The capsule is a compact continuation summary, not a full transcript or general document-search index.

hosts.other_mcp_limit: Structural tool access may work; no universal promise of automatic memory ingestion or native sidebar, notifications and capsule injection.
hosts.validation_status: Protocol interoperability and real-host end-to-end installation are distinct checks. See the host matrix for each supported or unverified combination.

architecture.distribution: One local installation includes engine executable, structural tool dependencies, OpenCode plugin, skills and a bundled MCP stdio server.
architecture.runtime: Local Rust engine with local state storage; TypeScript/JavaScript host adapters and structural tools.
architecture.persistence: .openstate/state.jsonl within the repository, or a supported symlink/pointer arrangement when filesystem constraints require it.
architecture.model_interaction: No language model is required to infer stored state facts; the engine derives facts from observed events. The coding agent itself remains external.
architecture.data_flow: Host events or stored-session replay -> adapter -> local state engine -> fact store -> reports/capsule. Structural tool preview -> apply -> Rust commit boundary -> project files.
architecture.authentication: A paid license is validated by the licensing layer; trial applies are counted by the trial license service.
architecture.installer: Installer verifies platform assets and release checksums/signatures; local executable smoke checks are part of the intended release process.

privacy_security.telemetry: No analytics telemetry sent by the engine.
network_exceptions: Installer downloads distribution artifacts from GitHub.
Paid and trial licensing calls to Keygen and the OpenState license worker, including a license key or trial identity, a hashed machine fingerprint and platform name.
Configured host history access may contact a configured OpenCode API endpoint rather than only filesystem history.
privacy_security.data_recorded_locally: Project state can include user messages, command lines and paths; treat .openstate as sensitive shell history.
privacy_security.project_content_sent_to_license: None; project source, filenames and local state are not needed for licensing.
privacy_security.license_key_protection: Local license file outside project repository; paid machine limit and offline validation documented.
limitations: Closed-source engine, despite MIT licensing of some public integration surfaces
No assertion that every host or platform is runtime-verified
A model can still choose a wrong code change even when the edit operation is safe

frequently_asked_questions.question: Does OpenState make my agent write correct code?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: It validates structural mutation targets and refuses invalid preview/apply contracts. It does not replace semantic code review or tests.

frequently_asked_questions.question: Does it share memory between all machines?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: No. Project state remains local to one machine and repository; it is not a hosted team database.

frequently_asked_questions.question: Does every MCP host get automatic memory?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: No. OpenCode has native automatic capture and injection. Other hosts have tools and supported stored-session assessment on demand.

frequently_asked_questions.question: Do free users lose read tools after 30 edits?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: No. Reads, searches and previews remain available; only structural apply writes require payment after the free allowance.

frequently_asked_questions.question: Does the one-time license include version 1.x?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: No promise of 1.x access. It is for all 0.x releases.

frequently_asked_questions.question: Does OpenState upload my code?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: The project state and code tools run locally. License checks send licensing identifiers, not project code.

frequently_asked_questions.question: Which language model must I use?
frequently_asked_questions.answer: None in particular; it is local tooling for external coding agents and MCP hosts, not a model provider.
